name: White soft paraffin
className: Emollient (paraffin ointment); not a UK licensed single-ingredient medicine

availability.note: No UK product information for white soft paraffin alone as an ointment. Searched 2026-10-17: emc search by the clinic trade name, white soft paraffin and petroleum jelly, and the emc white soft paraffin ingredient page (only multi-ingredient emollient creams and an emulsifying ointment that is 50% white soft paraffin with emulsifying wax and liquid paraffin); MHRA Products index by product name and substance (white soft paraffin only appears in creams or ointments with other ingredients or as an excipient). Those products are not this product and their labels were not used. General fire-safety advice (not product information): the MHRA Drug Safety Update on emollients (December 2018) says there is a fire risk with all paraffin-containing emollients, regardless of paraffin concentration, because fabric in contact with an emollient or emollient-treated skin can rapidly ignite; patients should not smoke or go near naked flames. The SPS article on fire risk with emollients (June 2026) says people should keep using emollients as prescribed, change and wash clothing and bedding regularly, and take extra care with smoking, medical oxygen, reduced mobility or confusion.
